title: #NiUnaMenos at 11: Massive Protests Across 30+ Argentine Cities Against Femicide and Milei's Gender Policy Rollbacks
detail: On the 11th anniversary of the #NiUnaMenos movement — born June 3, 2015 in response to the femicide of 14-year-old Chiara Páez — thousands of Argentines marched in at least 30 cities, re-energized by the fresh murder of Agostina Vega (also 14). Demonstrators converged on the Congreso Nacional and the Obelisco in Buenos Aires and gathered in Córdoba, Rosario, Mendoza, Tucumán, Mar del Plata, and Neuquén. Protest signs demanded government accountability for femicide prevention and attacked President Milei's dismantling of gender-protection institutions: INADI (the anti-discrimination institute) was abolished in 2024; the Ministry of Women, Gender and Diversity was downgraded to a secretariat and then defunded; emergency hotlines for gender violence were shut or handed to NGOs without funding. Argentina's overall femicide statistics — a woman killed every 30 hours — have not improved under the Milei administration. The protests drew international attention as a test of popular resistance to Milei's social-conservative agenda ahead of October 2026 midterm elections.

media.caption: Thousands march on June 4, 2026 — NiUnaMenos anniversary — against femicide across Argentina
